claim: Versioned NVIDIA network exports adapt callbacks into a shared internal network API.
Common send dispatch validates communicator/output request and invokes the selected communicator send implementation.
Communicators retain endpoints and endpoints retain domains through shared ownership, while keyed caches use weak references.
Concrete SENDRECV uses a plugin MR wrapper and conditionally extracts its underlying fabric descriptor; historical common comments are not a null-wrapper guarantee.
The C loading test checks dlopen/dlclose of the configured built shared library, not peer payload correctness.
The pinned source exports ncclNetPlugin v6 through v12 tables and version-specific size/configuration wrappers.
v11/v12 initialization stores traffic-class context and reference-counts repeated calls around one common plugin initialization.
v10 payload wrappers contain TODO profiling-handle support and exported receive-consumed hooks are null.
Baseline network properties advertise host-driven net device type and derive CUDA/DMA-BUF pointer support from internal properties.
Static assertions bound connection-handle layout/size and expected request capacity against the interface limits.
Parameter initialization visits registered typed parameters and returns the first initialization error.
Plugin creation initializes page/cache alignment and topology/platform context before transport selection and complete_init.
complete_init separates selected resource creation from candidate protocol construction/probing.
A temporary endpoint selected with PID-mod-device and thread key permits concrete endpoint property/platform checks during initialization.
Unsupported GDR can trigger conservative NCCL SIMPLE configuration, separate from the selected plugin SENDRECV/RDMA protocol.
check_sources asserts DEFAULT/API/ENVIRONMENT provenance and check_late_set asserts rejected mutation after access.
Platform registration selects compiled policy candidates and initializes the selected platform before protocol construction.
AWS initialization supplies an EFA filter when FI_PROVIDER is absent and applies known-platform protocol defaults only under default provenance/EFA conditions.
An existing NCCL_TOPO_FILE is respected; endpoint configuration separately checks actual EFA GDR/native-write/ordering capabilities under guards.
NIC lists are sorted/grouped with quotient/remainder distribution and attached accelerator-group metadata.
Synthetic tests distinguish a shared PCIe switch from a shared host bridge and reject missing/disjoint topology objects.
check_gdaki_flags validates opt-in hardware-counter policy separately from successful device resource construction.
Explicit nondefault protocol selection takes a direct initializer branch and exits on failure rather than automatically changing protocols.
Default selection chooses usable multi-rail RDMA; otherwise it selects SENDRECV and deletes the other RDMA candidate, without the final single-rail fallback listed in a broad comment.
Provider discovery calls fi_getinfo, applies inclusion/TCP filters, and retains the selected provider/fabric match.
SENDRECV requests tagged reliable-datagram capabilities and negotiates memory support through guarded API queries.
RDMA requests message/RMA/HMEM and four bytes of CQ data, validates returned CQ size, and guards early completion by progress/eager compatibility.
Returned MR virtual-address, endpoint-binding, and data-progress modes affect later behavior; EFA has a provider-specific runtime version check.
Repeated nonblocking connect reuses the endpoint retained by handle state when its communicator already exists.
Connection envelopes carry local/remote connector IDs and connection endpoint information, with appended transport data.
SENDRECV connect/accept preserve incomplete state and return communicator outputs only after their handshake readiness path.
RDMA connection setup exchanges mailbox/key/endpoint data and rejects data/control rail-count mismatch.
ReuseListenCommTest copies the original exchanged handle each iteration because connect mutates local saved state.
Registration validates build-supported memory type and constructs ordinary or DMA-BUF keys with endpoint context.
Ordinary non-Neuron registration keys round address coverage to cache alignment, while Neuron skips that extension.
MR cache lookup checks covered page intervals and required endpoint identity, increments references, and does not implement an application allocation generation.
SENDRECV holds cache locking across miss/registration/insertion and rolls back newly registered handles if insertion fails.
del_entry returns zero while references remain and one after final removal to signal actual deregistration.
DMA-BUF viability checks build, disablement, device attributes, and kernel support before selected provider/HMEM/API support is considered.
MR tests cover subrange hits, overlap misses, duplicate insertion, reference decrements, final deletion, and alignment; endpoint scope is explicitly not exercised by that fixture.
Simple and registration-backed freelists have distinct backing ownership; callbacks may run under caller locks and destruction releases even unreturned entries.
SENDRECV increments inflight only after accepted posting and uses a false decrement flag when returning a pre-post failed slot.
RDMA request subclasses own typed post/completion/free responsibilities, per-rail contexts, counts, and child state.
post_with_pending_retry retains EAGAIN requests internally; repeated EAGAIN returns the request to the front and ends a progress pass.
ID pools allocate bitmap positions, return FI_KEY_NOTAVAIL on exhaustion, and reject invalid/double frees.
Freelist tests assert capacity, init/fini counts, lazy registered reserve, and already-satisfied reserve behavior.
SENDRECV posts its negotiated communicator tag rather than callback tags and advertises max_group_receives equal to one.
fi_tsend EAGAIN progresses CQ, returns null request, and retires the temporary slot without inflight decrement.
Payload CQ contexts recover requests, record receive actual length, and mark completion or error.
SENDRECV terminal test reports done and returns the request to its pool, so its pointer is no longer a live operation handle.
GroupedRecvTest skips counts above advertised maxRecvs, preserving the selected transport capability boundary.
Receive entries advertise destination offset/capacity/tag/index/sequence and per-rail registration keys through control mailboxes.
has_ctrl_msg validates ready sequence before trusting grouped count and uses acquire fences before dependent reads.
Ordinary sends without usable control return no request; scheduled segment posting advances the cursor only after accepted posts.
Remote-write immediate data maps to communicator, sequence, sub-receive index, and expected segment count before parent aggregation.
Eager data uses staging, ordered/tagged matching, copy children, and later control reconciliation; early completion is separately guarded by NCCL optional receive semantics.
Control tests assert structure/readiness/tag bounds including entries beyond num_recvs remaining invisible.
Forced rail expansion duplicates provider information cyclically and requires a multiple of actual entries; it does not create more physical NICs.
Control endpoint count can be one or all rails and remains distinct from data stripe scheduling.
Below the strict small-message threshold one rail is chosen with a separate rotation counter; larger messages use bounded stripe count and 128-byte aligned maximum sizes.
With four rails/minimum stripe 4096, an 8193-byte large-branch payload uses two stripes of 4224 and 3969 bytes.
Threshold tests compare expected rail IDs, offsets, lengths, boundary sizes, and rotation rather than achieved bandwidth.
CQ EAGAIN, posting EAGAIN, and readerr EAGAIN have different no-progress/acceptance meanings.
RDMA progresses CQ rails and pending requests; testing one request can advance unrelated requests sharing endpoint resources.
RDMA remote-write error handling avoids decoding unreliable CQ data and returns EIO rather than inventing a request context.
Successful RDMA test frees completed requests, while the shown request-error branch returns an error without using that same success free path.
SENDRECV flush can skip, invoke GPU flush, or post/test a fabric read according to capability/configuration.
poll_and_validate flushes CUDA receives but guards its final payload byte comparison with receiver rank and non-CUDA memory.
Tuner initialization can successfully return a null context for NCCL fallback; region is preferred over model when both are supported unless model is validly forced.
Versioned collective/chunk callbacks preserve fallback when a context/internal callback is absent.
Gin init requires initialized OFI NET, RDMA protocol, global-registration assumptions, and supported GDRCopy forced PCIe copy.
Direct GDAKI context validation rejects unsupported backend structure versions before resource construction and authorizes each used domain before GDA operations.
The symbol probe verifies proxy/direct export presence under HAVE_GDAKI without proving a fabric transfer.
The layout probe asserts clean rejection of null, negative, zero, and above-maximum backend versions before real communicator use.
Endpoint invalidation sets inactive and removes the endpoint from its domain cache; it does not mark the entire domain inactive.
Inflight SENDRECV close aborts endpoint resources before deleting request bookkeeping, without establishing successful payload delivery.
RDMA close queues inactive communicators for control/close/flush-aware cleanup and blocks on the final open send/receive close until cleanup completes or fails.
InflightCloseTest exercises interrupted deregistration/close and reconnect, without ordinary completion polling or successful payload-delivery validation.
Logging bridges to the supplied NCCL logger and TRACE macro emission is compile-time gated.
Trace correlation distinguishes callback output, pooled plugin request, and fabric context pointer roles.
